approachQuestion.prompt:
Market visits

An array price lists a positive unit price for successive days. Start with no item, may hold at most one item, may buy and sell repeatedly, and must finish with no item. There are no transaction fees, cooldowns or transaction limits. Return maximum total profit. Buying and selling at the same day price is allowed but yields zero.

Example 1: price=[5,2,4,3,7] → 6 by gains 2 and 4.
Example 2: price=[7,4,1] → 0.
Example 3: price=[2,2] → 0.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ price[i] ≤ 10^9. Input is read-only. Return only the stated scalar result. All arithmetic and comparisons use constant-time exact 64-bit operations; all intermediate values fit.

options.text: Scan adjacent days and sum max(0,price[i]-price[i-1]). Do not construct transactions.
options.feedback: Any held interval has profit equal to its sum of adjacent differences; including a negative difference cannot help when trades are unrestricted and free. All positive differences can be realized by joining consecutive rises into a holding interval.

options.text: Return the difference between the global maximum price and global minimum price, clamped at zero.
options.feedback: The minimum may occur after the maximum. For [5,2], this returns 3 although no profitable trade is possible.

options.text: Find only the single most profitable buy-then-sell pair.
options.feedback: A single transaction omits separate gains. For [1,3,1,3], two transactions yield 4 while one yields only 2.

options.text: Use iterative cash/hold state updates for each day, storing only the previous cash and hold values; return the final cash state.
options.feedback: This is equally optimal in time and space: cash is the best profit while holding nothing, and hold is the best profit while holding one item. The unrestricted daily choices reduce to the same profit as the positive-difference sum.

details: Scan adjacent days and sum max(0,price[i]-price[i-1]). Do not construct transactions.

Every positive adjacent rise contributes attainable profit when repeated trades have no added constraints in this task. Summing positive rises equals buying at each valley and selling at its next peak. Fees or cooldowns would require different state.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed frontier method, regardless of your previous choice. Use exactly the frontier method above as iterative scans with scalar indices, counters and accumulators. Do not copy the input and do not store a decision list. Let n be the number of input records or positions. Choose the tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Input and returned scalar are excluded. All other live storage, including copying and any call stack, is counted. No hashing or expected-time operations are used.

feedback.reason: Scan adjacent prices and retain only accumulated profit.

messages.text: The method stores no per-item history or copied input.
The scans do not restart for each item.
In the worst case every input item can affect the answer.

details: There are n-1 adjacent differences, each processed once with constant arithmetic. This gives O(n) worst-case time. One accumulated profit and the current adjacent values use O(1) space; no transaction list is built.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The method stores no per-item history or copied input.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(1)”: The scans do not restart for each item.
“Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1)”: In the worst case every input item can affect the answer.
